title: Essential image descent for a normalized native functor
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime and $X$ a Noetherian finite-dimensional scheme with $\ell$ invertible in every local ring. Let $D$ be a normalized native functor of [def-sf-locally-finite-adic-normalized-functor]. For every native derived object $M$, bounded adic constructibility holds if and only if $M$ is isomorphic to $D.JA$ for some source object $A$.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(1),(2), split from native realization proof steps 3, 6 and 7.

proof.text: Compare bounded constructibility with the condensed finite-stage category using the internal-module and section-module equivalences and the local-freeness theorems. The object clause of the condensed filtered two-colimit descends any native bounded constructible object to a finite stage. Essential surjectivity of the finite-field realization lifts that stage to a source object, and tensor transitivity identifies its normalized image with the original object. The forward direction follows because finite realization and scalar extension preserve bounded constructibility.
